title: Likes and feelings — sentences where the person is the owner
title_target: আমার ভালো লাগে — a-mar bha-lo la-gé
goal: Say what you like, don't like, feel like doing, and what you think — with a surprising structure: the one who feels stands as the owner, and the feeling becomes the subject of the sentence.
bekal: use আমার ভালো লাগে for “I like”
tell it apart from আমি ভালোবাসি
say আমার ইচ্ছে করছে (I feel like …)
give an opinion with আমার মনে হয়
name feelings: খুশি, ক্লান্ত, রাগ, ভয়

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — Evening on the roof, listening to a song
dialogs.intro: Mitali plays a Rabindra Sangeet song on her phone. Watch the structure of “I like”: the person who feels appears in the possessive — আমার — not as the subject.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: How do you like this song?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I really like it. Whose song is it?
lines.literal: to-me — very — good — is-feeling. whose — song?

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Rabindranath's. We call it Rabindra Sangeet.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: It reminds me of Indonesian kroncong.
lines.literal: my — Indonesia's — kroncong's — matter — mind-in — is-falling.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Really? What kind of songs do you like?
lines.literal: so? your — what — kind-of — song — liking?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I like slow songs. I don't like loud ones.
lines.literal: slow — song — liking. loud — song — good — feel — not.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Me too. At dusk I feel like listening to songs.
lines.literal: mine-too — so. dusk-at — song — to-hear — wish — happens.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I think Bengali is a very melodious language.
lines.literal: my — mind-in — happens — Bengali — language-the — very — melodious.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: I'm glad to hear it! We love this language.
lines.literal: hearing — glad — became! we — language-the-to — love.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I understand. After February 21, I understood.
lines.literal: understand. Ekushey — February's — after — I — have-understood.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Are you feeling tired? Shall I bring tea?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: No, no, I actually feel good. Play one more song.
lines.literal: no — no, to-me — good-indeed — is-feeling. one-more — song — give-please.

notes: **This is Bengali's most characteristic structure: the one who feels stands as the OWNER, not the subject.** আমার ভালো লাগে means “I like it”, but literally “**to me** it feels good”. The subject of the sentence is **the feeling**, while the person appears in the possessive: আমার, আপনার, তার. ⚠️ So never say *আমি ভালো লাগি* — that means “I feel nice to others”.

**The same structure handles a whole group of meanings:** আমার ভালো লাগে (I like it), আমার ক্লান্ত লাগছে (I'm tired), আমার খিদে পেয়েছে (I'm hungry), আমার ঠান্ডা লাগছে (I'm cold), আমার ভয় করছে (I'm scared), আমার মনে হয় (I think), আমার মনে পড়ছে (I remember). Once you recognize the pattern, the whole group opens up at once.

⚠️ **ভালো লাগে and ভালোবাসি are different and not interchangeable.** **ভালো লাগে** is for ordinary liking that can change — food, songs, weather, places. **ভালোবাসি** is for deep love — people, homeland, language. আমি তোমাকে ভালোবাসি is “I love you”, and saying it to a bowl of noodles sounds like a joke. When in doubt, use ভালো লাগে.

**পছন্দ *pôchhôndô* is a safe third option.** আমার এটা পছন্দ (I like this), আপনার কী পছন্দ? (what do you like?). The word comes from Persian and feels more neutral than the other two — good for stating a taste without involving feelings.

**ইচ্ছে করছে means “I feel like …”, and it also uses the owner form.** আমার ঘুমাতে ইচ্ছে করছে (I feel like sleeping), আমার চা খেতে ইচ্ছে করছে (I feel like having tea). ⚠️ Note that the verb uses the **-তে** form from Unit 12: the desired action stands in front, the wish at the end.

**মন *môn* means “heart-mind”, and it gives rise to a group of expressions that can't be translated word for word.** মনে হয় (it seems, I think), মনে পড়ে (comes to mind), মনে আছে (I remember), মনে রাখা (to keep in mind), মন খারাপ (sad — literally “bad heart”), মন ভালো (happy). ⚠️ **মন খারাপ** is the most common way to express sadness, and knowing it lets you ask after someone sincerely: **মন খারাপ?**

**রবীন্দ্রনাথ ঠাকুর — Rabindranath Tagore — is everywhere in Bengali life.** He wrote over two thousand songs called **রবীন্দ্রসঙ্গীত**, and they are sung at weddings, funerals, protests and on rooftops in the evening. ⚠️ Mentioning him with respect — people usually say **রবীন্দ্রনাথ** or **কবিগুরু** (teacher of poets) — will open a warm conversation with almost anyone.

grammars.title: Feeling sentences: owner + feeling + verb
after: ⚠️ **The verb is always in the সে form** — লাগে, পেয়েছে, করছে, হয় — because the subject is the feeling, not the person. This holds whoever the owner is: আমার লাগে, আপনার লাগে, তার লাগে. Nothing changes except the possessive word in front.

grammars.title: Feelings and opinions
after: ⚠️ **চিন্তা means “worry” far more often than “thought”** — an easy trap. **চিন্তা করবেন না** means “don't worry”, and saying it to someone who is anxious is a kindness, not a brush-off.

blocks.title: Three Bengali things worth having an opinion on
items: **রবীন্দ্রসঙ্গীত and নজরুলগীতি** — the two great song traditions, of Rabindranath Tagore and Kazi Nazrul Islam. Saying you like one opens a long conversation; mentioning both makes you sound like a host, not a guest.
**সত্যজিৎ রায়** *sôtôjit ray* — Satyajit Ray, the Bengali director whose films are known worldwide. His films are slow, quiet and deeply human; Bengalis are very proud of him.

**আড্ডা** *aDDa* — long, aimless chatting at a tea stall or on a rooftop, for hours. ⚠️ It isn't just chatting; it's considered a real cultural activity, and turning down an invitation to আড্ডা again and again feels like turning down friendship.

blocks.text: One sentence worth learning whole: **আপনার সঙ্গে কথা বলে ভালো লাগল** — “it was nice talking to you”. It uses this unit's pattern, and it's a warm way to part after a first conversation with anyone. Say it sincerely at the end of an আড্ডা and you'll most likely be invited back.

items: Like this song: এই গানটা আমার ____ ।

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: ভালো লাগে — ভালোবাসি — ভালো লাগে — ভালোবাসি
আমার বাংলা গান ভালো লাগে। — আমার ঝাল ভালো লাগে না। — আমার ঘুরতে ইচ্ছে করছে। — আমার মনে হয় ঠিক আছে। — আমার খিদে পেয়েছে।
আমার এই গানটা ভালো লাগে। — আমার ঝাল ভালো লাগে না। — আমার খিদে পেয়েছে। — আমার চা খেতে ইচ্ছে করছে। — আমার মনে হয় ভালো। — আমার বাড়ির কথা মনে পড়ছে।
